body:
The GPU (graphics processor) sorter used primitive integers for item counts,
key widths and other quantities with different meanings. Its migration also
needs to reach unchanged producers and consumers so those contracts remain
consistent across complete operations.

The published change introduces sorting quantities for counts, widths, passes
and digits. The continuation covers retained capacities, byte layouts and the
bounding volume hierarchy (BVH), vertex normals, cloth self-collision,
underlayers, hair, fitting and their application consumers.

Sorting populations remain distinct from #779's launch quantities. The work
consumes the canonical invocation, workgroup, buffer-byte and element-stride
owners. Shared GPU submission, copying, readback and error handling are
coordinated with #826 through explicit whole-function ownership. Compatibility
adapters and competing implementations are outside the intended final API.

## Current status

This pull request remains a draft. Its published head is
`e14407cc494615f0b16522fb7aa7672a3589a3c3`. The audit continuation is local;
its latest local commit is `ead46619dec5ef45993f63202cb289bd3986b018`.
No continuation code has been pushed or submitted for hosted checks.
Current main was reconfirmed as `990430b77a9f63548ffcb642074185f61ddb3322`;
#779 remains at `71f9cab8a5f97760e2e61ca4c74876b715f8aebc`.

Local implementation now includes:

- Checked sorting and dispatch layouts, scratch growth and exact input byte
  prefixes. Recorded BVH views retain their actual buffers and layout, and a
  replacement collider is published only after its initial submission succeeds.
- Canonical submission, ranged copying and validation-scope consumers. Grouped
  readback retains its producing device and concrete callback and polling
  causes. Armor and fitting readbacks use named tickets and logical prefixes;
  empty numeric reductions return a typed error.
- Metal tile and engraving admission, immutable recipe association and checked
  texture-map extents. Generated resource programs use explicit entry points,
  canonical texture component projection and fallible storage-format spelling.
- Sealed host and native strand shapes, source and device association, full
  storage admission before resident-prefix selection, checked native identities
  and work arrays, and source-bound simulation frames. Card geometry preserves
  the distinction between generic triangle lists and generated strips. Atlas
  recipes and actual mip metadata flow through their owning builders.
- The coordinated renderer receiver, including actual source identity, typed
  selection and frame populations, logical binding prefixes and fallible
  simulation updates. Receiving review exposed and resolved duplicate error
  conversion, unit-import and unused-binding integration findings.
- One shared mesh strip owner used by the host card builder and the Creator's
  card and ribbon paths. The Creator carries typed form ordinals, shares,
  counts and distances through preview, export and existing fixtures. Empty
  strand sources draw zero strands, logical reads exclude allocation padding,
  and strip submission errors propagate. Atlas export reads each mip's actual
  dimensions. Scoped Code, Rule and Comment Reviews found no remaining finding
  after corrections; source comparisons preserve all four strip WGSL programs
  and the existing fixture oracles.
- Fixed scalp mip layouts remain attached to the actual buffer and creating
  device through baking, readback and preview upload. Texel spans, shadow block
  counts, storage records, byte addresses and launches have separate owners.
  Foreign-device host reads reject before mapping. Host texture reads await the
  canonical mapping future. Exact source comparisons
  preserve shader text, mip addresses, pass order and existing fixture oracles;
  all three scoped reviews and the thirteen-lens scoped successor are clear.
- Creator initialization caches and material/clothing receivers preserve their
  actual error causes. Mail textures are all decoded before image handles or a
  successful cache entry are published. Hair completion uses the canonical
  fallible asynchronous completion API. Mesh strip row admission preserves its
  integer-conversion cause. The two-dimensional Advect program relies on the
  native sRGB sample conversion once, and its three-dimensional Clamp path
  bounds the upper texture address. Each code family has scoped independent
  Code, Rule and Comment Review evidence. A nested lockfile also records its
  declared armor dependencies; final locked hosted validation remains pending.

- Metal device acquisition, baking and readback now use one direct async API.
  The Creator shares its async armor initialization cache and retains the first
  completed result, including its original error. Texture export awaits that
  path; native offline preview, export and existing fixtures wait at their
  application boundaries. Scalp texture reads and the longest-strand readback
  also await the canonical buffer mapping owner. Shader text, numerical bodies
  and existing fixture oracles are preserved by exact source comparisons.
- A scalp is returned only after its final boundary submission succeeds.
  Hairline projection considers every triangle instead of assuming all triangles
  fit an unsupported first-corner distance bound. Documentation now describes
  the actual workgroup scheduling, batching, scratch reuse and approximate head
  field, with moved guide-map documentation attached to its owning method.

- Metal texture-density scaling now belongs to GeneratedArmor. It admits
  complete triangles, matching finite geometry and UV columns, checked indices
  and finite replacement coordinates before any mutation. The existing edge
  weighting and arithmetic order are preserved. Armory retains pending,
  successful and failed fits with actual error causes; a later preview failure
  no longer destroys a successful fitted mesh.
- Rigged export carries one per-vertex UV column. Plate maps retain only image
  identity, so compaction cannot reuse an original, unselected UV slice after
  geometry is compacted. Both character and equipment exporters consume the
  final API. Texture precedence and existing fixture oracles are preserved.
  Each of these two increments has fresh thirteen-lens source review and
  independent Code, Rule and Comment Review on its exact local sources.

- Canonical encoded color and named surface appearance now flow through all
  reviewed material defaults, catalog and textile producers, retained garment
  and export records, preview renderers and native artifact consumers. Components
  retain one appearance choice: inheritance, scalar factors or the actual textile
  recipe. Both review-JSON producers use one checked native component projection;
  GLB selects the effective texture factor before checking linear color. Body
  preview and GLB share one skin source. Existing fixture values and oracles are
  preserved. Fresh scoped thirteen-lens, Code, Rule and Comment Reviews are clear
  on the exact 77-file local increment; this is source evidence only.

These are local source-review results. They establish no compiled, runtime or
whole-PR acceptance. The complete combined source still needs a fresh
post-repair wave across all thirteen lenses.

Required implementation remains in physical and grid producers, body and
fitting, armor and runtime consumers, and the lower GPU composition. Material
lengths, counts, seeds, engraving roles, trim operations and typed application
validation and absence errors remain open. Export admission also needs typed
violations, finite body geometry and checked GLB chunk/container lengths. The
completed scalar-appearance, density, Armory and UV increments do not clear
those connected responsibilities.

Native scalp work still requires coherent source, device, lattice, root and
boundary admission; the async texture changes do not certify the complete
browser grooming or studio workflow. Reviewed native and generated-program
source packets from #826 still require canonical core callers, exports and
lockfiles to be composed and reviewed together. Fresh receiving review has
also identified retained native API and error-ownership gaps. These dependencies
remain open; earlier scoped reviews do not waive them.

Bruno transferred the remaining connected #774 claims to this coordinated
continuation. The [ownership record](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774#issuecomment-6372371468)
supersedes the earlier missing-implementer limitation. #826 owns the agreed lower
GPU helpers, generated Map/Gather/Scatter/Stencil/Stream programs and fluid
pipelines, armor native functions, hair renderer and selection-policy family.
#780 owns sorting and reduction, extraction, the connected physical producers,
layouts, fitting and application errors. The Metal acquisition/read functions
and their async callers were explicitly transferred to #780. Shared-function
changes require an agreed owner; ownership does not establish implementation
clearance.

## Validation

No new tests, test cases, test helpers, assertions or documentation tests are
added by the continuation. Existing fixture API changes follow the canonical
migration while retaining their cases and oracles. Project checks will use the
hosted workflows after connected migration families are complete.

The ignored source-backed ledger records all thirteen lenses, contracts,
dispositions, dependencies, repairs and acceptance criteria. Discovery,
implementation and validation remain distinct. Targeted source comparisons and
scoped reviews do not substitute for complete post-repair audit waves.

Completion requires all thirteen lenses, final independent Code Review, Rule
Review and Comment Review, and required hosted CI to pass on the same final
pushed revision. Those gates remain pending. Do not merge.

## Implementation context

Material decisions are separate sorting and launch quantities, canonical shared
owners, checked layouts before recording, actual source and provider association,
retained native causes, and explicit whole-function ownership across #774 and
#826. Source preservation evidence is kept separate from pending hosted
acceptance. No reviewed shared conversation snapshot is available for this
continuation; this description is the authoritative scope and validation summary.

Part of #726. Related dispatch API: #779. Shared receiving contracts: #826.
